title: [Livestream 14/12/2024] Going to the cinema
prompt: The graph shows the percentage of people visiting the cinema once a month or more between 1984 and 2003 (4 age groups). Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph gives information about the proportion of people of different age groups going to the movies at least one time per month from 1984 to 2003.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, it is clear that the popularity of going to the cinema went up during the period shown among all four age brackets, with the 15-24 group doing so the most, while those above 35 years old had the least interest.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at younger individuals, in 1984, around 18% of those from 15 to 24 had the habit of visiting the cinema, far higher than the youngest group, 7-14, at 10%. An upward trend was recorded for the former group, with its figures rising to around 32% in 1992, before fluctuating and peaking at approximately 57% in 2003. A similar increasing tendency was seen in the 7-14 age bracket, as the numbers rose to 18% in 1992, continued climbing to reach 30% in 2003.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the other groups, there were around 4% of 25-to-35-year-olds and 1% of people older than that going to the cinema at least once a month in 1984. The younger bracket's numbers increased significantly to a quarter (25%) in 2003, despite some fluctuations from 1996 to 2000, while those for the older group did so far less significantly, rising to only about 12% in 2003.
